correctness.rationale: Independently checked the repaired dimensional scope and census. Any four-cycle in the cube flips each coordinate an even number of times; with distinct vertices the four steps alternate between two coordinates. Every matching is a bijection from even to odd vertices which respects Hamming adjacency, so the independent replay's checks of 2!, 4!, and 8! bijections are exhaustive for d=2,3,4. Enumerating opposite pairs in all coordinate squares generates precisely the defined reversible moves. The separate replay found the same vertex and edge counts, components, degree histogram, all-source eccentricities and 384-element cube group orbit of isolates. Its seed checks show that each displayed seed is a frozen perfect matching and all four are pairwise edge-disjoint. These checks support the general proof: the product decomposition Q_4 × Q_(d-4) yields independently chosen frozen matchings on all slices; squares with only outer directions have no matched edges, inner-only squares are frozen locally, and a mixed square needs the same inner edge in opposite-parity slices, which cross-disjointness forbids. Restricting the global matching to individual slices recovers all 2^(d-4) binary choices. The corrected minimality follows from the absence of isolates at d=2,3 and their existence at d=4; d=1 is explicitly exceptional and Q_0 has a single vertex.
residual_risks: The replay of the family in dimensions 4–7 is a finite check, not the argument for arbitrary d; the latter uses the coordinate-square cases. The lower bound is not an exact frozen-state census for higher dimensions.

originality.rationale: The repaired distinct claim relative to the older literature is the exact square-only graph structure at Q_4 and the parity-slice construction yielding a quantitative bound in all d≥4. The older cited graph and tiling results do not contain this structure; the raw matching counts were already tabulated and carry no originality. Multiple later-dated indexed records have genuine, in one case nearly complete, mathematical overlap, including identical base states and ingredient-level coverage of the bound. They are explicitly credited rather than treated as distinct advances on the common content. No earlier occurrence of those overlapping statements was verified; no historical priority or independence is inferred from catalogue dates.
residual_risks: The catalogue overlap is substantial and its shared seed data do not establish provenance or independent discovery. No evidence located makes those later-dated statements earlier coverage of the frozen entry.
A general primary literature lookup was not productive; indexed coverage is not assumed exhaustive.

Local dimer dynamics and shared indexed statements compared under originality
value.rationale: The local four-cycle move is a natural connectivity rule for dimers. At the first nonvacuous dimension with freezing, the result distinguishes a single mobile component from symmetry-equivalent frozen states and gives exact travel distances within the mobile component. Those exact local quantities cannot be read off the raw perfect-matching total or larger-cycle connectivity theorems. The disjoint-seed construction additionally certifies a doubly exponential family of isolated states in arbitrary dimension rather than an incidental small census alone.
residual_risks: No conclusion about the proportion of frozen states or connectivity of mobile states for d>4. Do not credit the Q_1 exception, raw matchings counts or later-duplicated statements as independent advances.
